headline: Bond vigilantes, Gulf oil shock and Taiwan quarantine lock in a lost, repressed half-decade

events: French government falls over budget; OAT-Bund spread blows out past 200bp and ECB activates TPI amid legal challenge from Germany's constitutional court
UK gilt 30-year yield tops 6.2% after fiscal event, forcing emergency spending cuts and a pension-fund collateral scramble
US tariff escalation with China and partial EU retaliation; global trade volumes fall 1.5%
Record northern-hemisphere heatwave and Indian monsoon failure push food prices up 18%
AI capex boom continues but hyperscaler margins compress; first large Nasdaq correction of 22%
Israel-Iran war re-escalates; tanker attacks and mining near Hormuz send Brent to $145 for three months
G20 inflation peaks near 6.9%; Fed hikes back to 5.25% while ECB is paralysed between inflation and periphery spreads
Weak US 10-year and 30-year Treasury auctions trigger a 'term premium shock'; 10-year yield hits 6.1% during a contested election year
Egypt, Pakistan, Kenya and Argentina enter default or distressed restructuring; IMF resources stretched thin
Europe rations gas in winter; German industrial output falls 7%
Global recession: world growth 0.6%, unemployment peaks at 6.5%; commercial property and private-credit losses hit regional banks
China imposes a customs 'quarantine' on Taiwan for 11 weeks; US-allied naval escort standoff; chip prices triple and export controls go total
Fed restarts asset purchases under 'market functioning' label and Treasury shifts issuance to bills; financial repression era begins
Bangladesh cyclone and Pakistani floods displace 30 million; Sahel-to-Mediterranean migration surge feeds far-right gains in Europe
AI firms push automation of back-office and customer service as a cost-cutting response; white-collar layoffs accelerate
Italy requires a hybrid ECB-ESM backstop with conditions; mass protests in Rome and Paris; Japan's BoJ caps JGB yields again as yen slides past 190
Geomagnetic storm damages high-voltage transformers in Quebec and Scandinavia, causing weeks-long regional blackouts
Energy security drive makes solar, batteries and nuclear life-extension national priorities; renewables installations hit record despite high capital costs
Sudan-Chad regional war and a Serbia-Kosovo armed crisis add to conflict count; Ukraine frozen along an armed ceasefire line
Global recovery is weak (2.3%); real wages in advanced economies still below 2026 levels
Inflation settles near 4% with policy rates held below it; savers quietly expropriated while debt ratios stabilise around 109% of GDP
Trade organised into US-led, China-led and non-aligned 'connector' blocs; WTO dispute system formally abandoned
AI adoption reaches 31% of firms; cumulative ~46 million jobs displaced, concentrated in clerical, call-centre and junior professional roles
Wave of populist governments elected across Europe and Latin America on platforms of capital controls, price caps and anti-migration policy
1.6C of warming locked in; insurers withdraw from large parts of Florida, southern Europe and coastal Asia

winners: Commodity and energy exporters with fiscal space (Gulf states outside the war zone, Norway, Australia, Canada)
Defence, grid and battery manufacturers and owners of AI compute capacity
Connector economies such as India, Vietnam, Mexico, Turkey and Morocco that arbitrage between blocs
Indebted homeowners with fixed-rate mortgages and governments that benefit from negative real rates
losers: Savers, pensioners and bondholders eroded by financial repression
Import-dependent low-income countries in debt distress, especially in Africa and South Asia
European energy-intensive industry and Southern European welfare states under conditionality
Young white-collar entrants and renters facing AI displacement and unaffordable housing
bullets: Public debt has stabilised near 109% of world GDP only because central banks tolerate inflation above policy rates; financial repression is the quiet consensus.
The 2028 Gulf oil shock and the 2029 Taiwan quarantine turned bloc rivalry into hard decoupling of chips, energy and payments systems.
A 2029 global recession pushed unemployment to 6.5%; the recovery is shallow and real wages in rich countries are still below 2026 levels.
Nine sovereign debt crises, including emerging-market defaults and an Italian bailout under joint ECB-ESM conditions, have strained the IMF and the euro.
Companies use AI mainly to cut costs during the downturn: 31% of firms use it in production, and about 46 million jobs have been displaced, mostly in clerical work.
Energy security, not climate policy, drives a record build-out of solar, batteries and nuclear, but warming reaches about 1.6C and disaster losses keep rising.
Trust in institutions is at a record low and unrest is high; populist governments promising price caps, capital controls and migration curbs dominate elections.
The world is organised into rival trade and payment blocs, with a non-aligned 'connector' tier taking a growing share of manufacturing.
wildcard: A severe geomagnetic storm in 2030 destroyed high-voltage transformers in Quebec and Scandinavia, causing weeks-long blackouts and a global scramble for grid hardware.
image_description: In a sweltering Marseille apartment in 2031, a family uses a rooftop battery to run one fan while a phone shows a ration-style electricity tariff, an AI benefits chatbot and live footage of protesters outside the shuttered local tax office.
